summary.text: Brian Burnett is a Republican member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 12-Position 1, in office since January 13, 2025, and he is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Stacy Willoughby.
Before joining the Legislature he spent more than 25 years in law enforcement, including 12 years as the elected sheriff of Chelan County.

paragraphs.text: Burnett spent more than 25 years in law enforcement before the Legislature, including 12 years as Chelan County's elected sheriff, according to his House Republican biography.

He has served as president of the Washington Association of Sheriffs and Police Chiefs and the Washington State Sheriffs' Association, and as a commissioner of the Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission, appointed by the governor.
He is director of law enforcement services for Seattle's Finest Security and Traffic Control and the administrative liaison for the Washington State Sheriffs' Association.
Burnett succeeded Republican Keith Goehner in the 12th District seat.
His biography says he serves on the Civil Rights and Judiciary, Community Safety, Early Learning and Human Services, and Appropriations committees and is the Assistant Republican Whip.
He and his wife, April, have been married 38 years, raised seven children in Wenatchee and have 13 grandchildren, the same biography says.
